verdict: No fatal or major error: every number of Parts C and D agrees with the engine/refuter/audit data, and the corrected Part D theory is used throughout. Findings are minor statements stronger than or different from the evidence, one wrong example, two imprecise proof sentences, and markup.

findings.claim: Every invariant local functional of degree -1 with three legs has Weyl weight at least 9/2, "the lowest being lambda^*AA".
findings.evidence: lambda^*AA has a single spinor leg, odd under -1 in Spin(4,C) (the argument of the proof of lem:c9-legs), so it carries no invariant. Exhaustive count of degree -1 three-leg sets: without derivatives (A^*,A,A) [3 vector indices of V, or one of V, or three of W_R^perp], (lambda^*,lambda,A) [lambda^* (x) lambda contains neither (2,2;1) nor (1,1;6)], (c^*,c,A) [one vector index] and (lambda^*,lambda^*,c) [no Spin(4)xSU(4) singlet in Sigma^* (x) Sigma^*] all have weight 5 and no invariant; the first invariants have weight 6: (A^*,lambda,lambda), (A^*|_V,A^*|_V,c) without derivatives and the four weight-5 sets with one derivative. The conclusion (no degree -1, weight-4 three-leg functional) is unaffected.

findings.by: Every invariant local functional of degree $-1$ with three legs has Weyl weight at least $6$, so these four functionals
